description: Practice speaking out loud: describe pictures, tell stories, explain how things work, and share your opinion with reasons.

A.studentGoal: I can say what I see in a picture using words and short sentences.

info.headline: Say it out loud: words, phrases, and first sentences.
info.summary: Starting speakers name things, describe pictures with short sentences, tell a simple story in order, and share what they like. Sentence frames, word banks, and pictures help every answer, and every try counts.
canDo: I can name people, places, and things in a picture.
I can tell what someone is doing with a short sentence.
I can tell a picture story with first, next, and last.
I can say what I like and give one reason with because.

categories.title: Describe a Picture
categories.desc: Say what you see and what people are doing.

categories.title: Tell a Story and Explain Steps
categories.desc: Tell what happened and how things work, in order.

categories.title: Share Opinions and Ask
categories.desc: Say what you like and why, and ask for help.

activities.title: What Do You See at Recess?
activities.skill: Describe people and actions in a picture
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the playground. Plan, then record your answer.
activities.prompt: Tell what you see on the playground. Who is there? What are they doing?

picture.alt: A busy playground with a tall slide, two swings, a tree, and a basketball hoop. Five kids wait in a long line for the slide. One girl swings, and the other swing is empty. Two boys play with a ball near the hoop. A teacher stands by the tree.

vocabulary: a tall toy you climb up and slide down
tobogán: juego alto que subes y por el que te deslizas
a seat that hangs and moves back and forth
columpio: asiento que cuelga y se mueve hacia adelante y atrás
people standing one behind the other
fila: personas paradas una detrás de otra
activities.responsePlaceholder: I see ___. The kids are ___ing.

models.A: I see kids. They are on the slide.
models.B: I see five kids in a line for the slide. A girl is on the swing, and two boys play with a ball.
models.C: I see a busy playground at recess. First, there are five kids waiting in a long line for the slide. Next to them, a girl is swinging, but the other swing is empty. Two boys are playing with a ball near the basketball hoop. A teacher stands by the tree, so everyone is safe.

activities.correct: Great describing! You named things and told what people are doing. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Point to one person. Say who it is and what the person is doing: A girl is swinging.
activities.support: Model: I see a slide. Kids are in a line. A girl is on the swing.
activities.extension: Tell which place on the playground you would go to first and why.

teacher.use: Warm-up for picture description; the most common ACCESS speaking task.
teacher.function: Describe people and actions with present progressive verbs.
teacher.lower: Student points and names: slide, swing, ball. Teacher expands into a sentence for the student to repeat.
teacher.onLevel: Student says 2 sentences with I see … and … is ___ing.
teacher.challenge: Student uses a location word: next to, near, behind.
teacher.noTech: Print the picture; partners take turns pointing and saying one sentence each.
teacher.prompt: What is the girl doing? Who is waiting?

activities.title: A Visit to the Library
activities.skill: Describe a place and what people do there
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the library. Plan, then record your answer.
activities.prompt: Tell about the library. What do you see? What are the people doing?

picture.alt: A library with tall bookshelves full of books. A boy reads a book on a green beanbag chair. At the front desk, a librarian helps a girl check out a book. A plant sits on a small table.

vocabulary: a place where you can borrow books
biblioteca: lugar donde puedes pedir libros prestados
the person who helps you find books
bibliotecario: la persona que te ayuda a encontrar libros
take a book home for a short time
sacar (un libro): llevar un libro a casa por un tiempo corto
activities.responsePlaceholder: I see ___. The boy is ___.

models.A: I see books. A boy reads.
models.B: I see shelves with a lot of books. A boy is reading on a green beanbag, and a girl is checking out a book.
models.C: This picture shows a quiet library with tall shelves full of books. A boy is reading on a comfy green beanbag chair. At the front desk, the librarian is helping a girl check out a book. I think the girl is happy because she can take her book home. There is also a plant on a small table.

activities.correct: Nice work! You described the place and the people. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Start with the place: I see a library. Then tell about one person.
activities.support: Model: I see a library. A boy is reading a book.
activities.extension: Tell what kind of book you would check out and why.

teacher.use: Language Arts tie-in: talk about reading places before a library visit.
teacher.function: Describe a place and people's actions.
teacher.lower: Student points to the shelf, boy, and librarian and repeats each name.
teacher.onLevel: Student says two connected sentences using and.
teacher.challenge: Student adds a feeling word with because.
teacher.noTech: Visit the school library and describe it to a partner.
teacher.prompt: Who helps the girl? What is the boy doing?

activities.title: Sunny Day, Rainy Day
activities.skill: Compare two pictures with weather words
activities.directions: Look at the two weather pictures. Plan, then record your answer.
activities.prompt: Tell about the weather in each picture. What are the kids wearing?

picture.alt: Two weather scenes. On the left, the sun shines in a blue sky and a boy in a T-shirt and shorts flies a kite. On the right, dark clouds drop rain, and a girl in a yellow raincoat and boots holds an umbrella next to a puddle.

vocabulary: soleado: cuando el sol está brillando
when water falls from the clouds
lluvioso: cuando cae agua de las nubes
a coat that keeps you dry in the rain
impermeable: abrigo que te mantiene seco bajo la lluvia
activities.responsePlaceholder: In this picture, it is ___. The ___ is wearing ___.

models.A: It is sunny. It is rainy.
models.B: In the first picture, it is sunny, and a boy is flying a kite. In the second picture, it is rainy, so the girl has an umbrella.
models.C: These two pictures show very different weather. On the left, it is sunny and warm, so the boy is wearing a T-shirt and shorts while he flies a kite. On the right, dark clouds are dropping rain. The girl is wearing a yellow raincoat and boots, and she holds an umbrella to stay dry. I would rather play outside on the sunny day because I love kites.

activities.correct: Good comparing! You used weather and clothes words. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Talk about one picture at a time. Say the weather first, then the clothes.
activities.support: Model: It is sunny. The boy has a kite. It is rainy. The girl has an umbrella.
activities.extension: Tell what you wear on a snowy day.

teacher.use: Science: weather unit; vocabulary for observing weather.
teacher.function: Describe and compare weather conditions.
teacher.lower: Student says one word for each picture: sunny, rainy. Teacher models a full sentence.
teacher.onLevel: Student describes both pictures using but or so.
teacher.challenge: Student explains why the clothes match the weather.
teacher.noTech: Hold up weather cards; students say It is ___ and act out the clothes.
teacher.prompt: What is the weather on the right? Why does the girl have an umbrella?

activities.title: Shapes on a Quilt
activities.skill: Name and count shapes
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the quilt. Plan, then record your answer.
activities.prompt: Tell what shapes you see on the quilt. How many of each shape are there?

picture.alt: A colorful quilt made of nine squares in three rows. Four squares have a red triangle, three squares have a yellow circle, and two squares have a blue rectangle.

vocabulary: a shape with 4 sides and 4 square corners
rectángulo: figura con 4 lados y 4 esquinas rectas
activities.responsePlaceholder: I see ___ triangles. There are ___ circles.

models.B: I see four red triangles and three yellow circles. There are two blue rectangles too.
models.C: The quilt has nine squares in three rows. I counted four red triangles, which is the most. There are three yellow circles and only two blue rectangles. Altogether, that is nine shapes, one in each square, because four plus three plus two equals nine.

activities.correct: Well done! You named shapes and counted them. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Touch each triangle and count out loud. Then do the circles.
activities.support: Model: I see 4 triangles. I see 3 circles. I see 2 rectangles.
activities.extension: Tell which shape there is the most of and how you know.

teacher.use: Math talk: geometry vocabulary and counting.
teacher.function: Describe attributes and quantities.
teacher.lower: Student points to a shape when the teacher says its name, then names it.
teacher.onLevel: Student names and counts all three shapes.
teacher.challenge: Student compares: There are more triangles than rectangles.
teacher.noTech: Use paper shapes; partners build a quilt and describe it.
teacher.prompt: How many triangles? Which shape has 3 sides?

activities.title: The Lost Dog
activities.skill: Tell a picture story in order
activities.directions: Look at the three pictures. Plan, then tell the story.
activities.prompt: Tell what happens in the story. Use first, next, and last.

picture.alt: A picture story in three parts. 1: A brown dog runs out of an open gate while a girl waters flowers. 2: The girl and her father put a Lost Dog poster on a tree. 3: A neighbor brings the dog back, and the girl hugs her dog.

sayFor: action words in the past (ran, put, brought)
vocabulary: a big paper with words and pictures that you hang up
cartel: papel grande con palabras e imágenes que cuelgas
a person who lives near you
vecino: persona que vive cerca de ti
activities.responsePlaceholder: First, ___. Next, ___. Last, ___.

models.A: The dog ran away. The girl is happy.
models.B: First, the dog ran out of the gate. Next, the girl and her dad put up a poster. Then a neighbor brought the dog back.
models.C: First, a girl was watering her flowers when her brown dog ran out of the open gate. Next, she and her dad made a Lost Dog poster and put it on a tree, because they wanted people to help. After that, a neighbor saw the poster and found the dog. Finally, the neighbor brought the dog home, and the girl gave it a big hug. She felt so happy!

activities.correct: Great storytelling! You told the story in order. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Point to picture 1 and say First. Point to picture 2 and say Next. Point to picture 3 and say Last.
activities.support: Model: First, the dog ran. Next, they made a poster. Last, the dog came home.
activities.extension: Tell how the girl felt in each picture.

teacher.use: Narrative speaking with a 3-panel sequence, like the ACCESS story task.
teacher.function: Narrate events in sequence.
teacher.lower: Student says one word or phrase per panel (dog runs, poster, hug); teacher recasts.
teacher.onLevel: Student uses first, next, last with one sentence per panel.
teacher.challenge: Student uses past tense and adds a feeling.
teacher.noTech: Cut the panels apart; students put them in order and retell.
teacher.prompt: What happened first? How did the dog come home?

activities.title: How a Plant Grows
activities.skill: Explain steps in a process
activities.directions: Look at the four pictures of the pots. Plan, then explain how the plant grows.
activities.prompt: Explain how a seed grows into a plant. Tell the steps in order.

picture.alt: Four pots in a row show how a plant grows. First, a seed is planted in the soil and watered. Next, a small sprout with two leaves comes up. Then, the plant grows taller with more leaves in the sun. Last, a yellow flower opens.

sayFor: plant words: seed, sprout, leaves, flower
vocabulary: the small part a new plant grows from
semilla: parte pequeña de donde crece una planta nueva
a very young plant that just came up
brote: planta muy joven que acaba de salir
tierra: suelo donde crecen las plantas
activities.responsePlaceholder: First, you ___. Then the seed ___.

models.B: First, you put a seed in the soil and give it water. Then a little sprout comes up. Last, it grows a flower.
models.C: Here is how a plant grows. First, you plant a seed in the soil and water it. Next, a small sprout with two leaves pushes up out of the soil. Then the plant gets taller and grows more leaves, because it gets sun and water. Finally, a yellow flower opens at the top.

activities.correct: Nice explaining! You told the steps in order. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Look at the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 under the pots. Say one step for each number.
activities.support: Model: First, plant the seed. Next, it grows a sprout. Then it gets big. Last, it has a flower.
activities.extension: Explain what a plant needs to stay alive.

teacher.use: Science: plant life cycle; process explanation.
teacher.function: Explain a process in order.
teacher.lower: Student uses the word bank and says seed, sprout, plant, flower in order.
teacher.onLevel: Student explains 3–4 steps with order words.
teacher.challenge: Student adds a because about sun or water.
teacher.noTech: Plant real seeds; students explain the steps they did.
teacher.prompt: What comes after the seed? What does the plant need?

activities.title: Classroom Jobs
activities.skill: Describe and explain a job
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the classroom. Plan, then record your answer.
activities.prompt: Tell what jobs the students are doing. Which job do you want?

picture.alt: A classroom where students do jobs. A boy feeds the fish in a fish tank, a girl waters a plant by the window, and another boy hands out papers at two desks. The teacher sits at her desk.

vocabulary: a task someone does to help
trabajo: tarea que alguien hace para ayudar
repartir: darle uno a cada persona
activities.responsePlaceholder: One student is ___. I want to ___ because ___.

models.B: A boy is feeding the fish, and a girl is watering the plant. I want to hand out papers because I like to help.
models.C: In this classroom, every student has a job. One boy is feeding the fish in the fish tank. A girl is watering the plant by the window, and another boy is handing out papers at the desks. I would like the fish job because I love animals. Also, the fish need food every day, so it is an important job.

activities.correct: Good job! You described the jobs and gave a reason. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Name one job first. Then say: I want to ___.
activities.support: Model: The boy feeds the fish. The girl waters the plant. I want to feed the fish.
activities.extension: Tell about a job you do at home.

teacher.use: Social & Instructional language: classroom routines and helping.
teacher.function: Describe actions and state a preference with a reason.
teacher.lower: Student points to a job and repeats the job name.
teacher.onLevel: Student describes two jobs and picks one with because.
teacher.challenge: Student explains why the job is important.
teacher.noTech: Use the class job chart; students say which job they have and what they do.
teacher.prompt: What is the girl doing? Which job would you pick?

activities.title: Shopping at the Market
activities.skill: Say what you like and why
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the market. Plan, then record your answer.
activities.prompt: What would you buy at this market? Tell why.

picture.alt: An outdoor community market with three stands. The fruit stand sells apples for 50¢ each and bananas. The vegetable stand sells corn for 25¢ each and carrots. The bread stand sells loaves of bread for $2 each. A seller stands behind each stand. A mother and her son buy apples, and a man carries a shopping bag.

vocabulary: a place where people sell food and other things
mercado: lugar donde la gente vende comida y otras cosas
comprar: pagar dinero para obtener algo
a small table or shop at a market
puesto: mesa o tienda pequeña en un mercado
activities.responsePlaceholder: I would buy ___ because ___.

models.B: I would buy apples because they are sweet. I like bananas too.
models.C: If I went to this market, I would buy apples from the fruit stand. One reason is that apples are sweet and crunchy, and they are healthy for me. Also, they only cost 50 cents each, so I could buy one for my brother too. After that, I would get bread for my family's dinner.

activities.correct: Nice opinion! You chose a food and gave a reason. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Point to a food you like. Say: I like ___ because it is ___.
activities.support: Model: I would buy corn because it is yummy.
activities.extension: Tell what your family likes to buy at the store.

teacher.use: Social Studies: community and markets; opinion with a reason.
teacher.function: Express a preference and support it with a reason.
teacher.lower: Student points and names a food; teacher models I like ___.
teacher.onLevel: Student gives an opinion with because.
teacher.challenge: Student gives two reasons with also.
teacher.noTech: Bring real or play food; students shop and say what they buy and why.
teacher.prompt: What would you buy? Why?

activities.title: Ask for Help
activities.skill: Ask a teacher for help politely
activities.directions: Read the problem. Plan, then record what you would say to your teacher.
activities.prompt: You do not understand the math directions. What do you say to your teacher?
vocabulary: entender: saber lo que algo significa
words that tell you what to do
instrucciones: palabras que te dicen qué hacer
activities.responsePlaceholder: Excuse me, ___. Can you please ___?

models.B: Excuse me, Ms. Lee. I don't understand the directions. Can you please say them again?
models.C: Excuse me, Ms. Lee, can I ask you a question? I read the math directions two times, but I still don't understand step two. Can you please show me an example? Then I can try the next problem by myself. Thank you!

activities.correct: Very polite! You told what you need and asked a question. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Start with Excuse me. End with please.
activities.support: Model: Excuse me. Can you help me, please?
activities.extension: Ask a classmate to help you with a word you don't know.

teacher.use: Social & Instructional survival language for the classroom.
teacher.function: Request help and clarification politely.
teacher.lower: Student repeats Excuse me, help please with a gesture.
teacher.onLevel: Student uses Excuse me + I don't understand + Can you please …?
teacher.challenge: Student names the exact part they need and thanks the teacher.
teacher.noTech: Role-play with a partner using frame cards.
teacher.prompt: What polite words did you use?

activities.title: Best Answer: The Garden
activities.skill: Choose a strong spoken description
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the school garden. Read the answers. Choose the strongest spoken answer.
activities.prompt: The teacher asks: What do you see in the garden?

picture.alt: A school garden with two wooden garden beds. Tomato plants grow in one bed, and tall sunflowers grow in the other bed. A girl waters the tomatoes with a watering can, and a boy digs with a small shovel. The school building is behind the garden.

sayFor: people and what they are doing
vocabulary: a place where people grow plants
jardín/huerto: lugar donde la gente cultiva plantas
regar: darles agua a las plantas
make a hole in the dirt
cavar: hacer un hoyo en la tierra

options.text: Garden.
I see a girl watering tomato plants and a boy digging.
Yes, I do.
The plants is.

activities.correct: Yes! This answer is a full sentence that tells who is there and what they are doing.
activities.hint: Find the answer that names people and tells what they are doing.
activities.support: Model: I see a girl watering tomato plants and a boy digging.
activities.extension: Say one more sentence about the sunflowers.

teacher.use: Shows students what a full spoken description sounds like.
teacher.function: Evaluate spoken descriptions.
teacher.lower: Teacher reads each answer aloud; student points to the one that matches the picture.
teacher.onLevel: Student chooses and repeats the strongest answer.
teacher.challenge: Student improves one of the weak answers.
teacher.noTech: Read the four answers aloud; students hold up a, b, c, or d cards.
teacher.prompt: Why is 'Garden.' not enough?

activities.title: Word or Full Sentence?
activities.skill: Tell a full spoken sentence from a single word
activities.directions: Read each answer. Sort it: is it a full sentence or just a word or two?
activities.prompt: A classmate answers the question: What do you do at recess? Sort each answer.
vocabulary: a group of words with a full idea
oración: grupo de palabras con una idea completa
recreo: tiempo de juego en la escuela

items.text: I play soccer with my friends.
At recess, I go down the slide.

activities.correct: Great sorting! Full sentences tell who and what they do.
activities.hint: A full sentence has a person (I, we, she) and an action (play, jump).
activities.support: Model: 'Soccer.' is a word. 'I play soccer.' is a sentence.
activities.extension: Change one short answer into a full sentence and say it aloud.

teacher.use: Builds awareness that spoken answers should be full sentences.
teacher.function: Distinguish complete from incomplete responses.
teacher.lower: Teacher reads each card aloud; student sorts with help.
teacher.onLevel: Student sorts all six cards.
teacher.challenge: Student fixes every short answer aloud.
teacher.noTech: Print the answers on strips for a pocket-chart sort.
teacher.prompt: How can you make 'Fun.' a full sentence?

activities.title: Best Answer: Favorite Season
activities.skill: Choose an answer with an opinion and a reason
activities.directions: Read the question and the answers. Choose the strongest spoken answer.
activities.prompt: The teacher asks: What season do you like best? Why?
vocabulary: one of the four parts of the year
estación: una de las cuatro partes del año

options.text: Summer.
I like it.
Winter is cold and summer.
I like summer best because I can swim at the pool.

activities.correct: Yes! This answer names a season and gives a reason with because.
activities.hint: Look for the answer that says the season AND why.
activities.support: Model: I like summer best because I can swim at the pool.
activities.extension: Say your own favorite season with a reason.

teacher.use: Opinion talk with a reason; modeling because.
teacher.function: Evaluate an opinion response.
teacher.lower: Teacher reads answers aloud; student finds the one with because.
teacher.onLevel: Student chooses and repeats the best answer.
teacher.challenge: Student gives an answer with two reasons.
teacher.noTech: Four corners: students go to a season corner and tell a partner why.
teacher.prompt: Which word shows the reason?

B.studentGoal: I can connect two or three sentences to describe, explain, or tell a story.

info.headline: Connect your ideas: and, because, then, so.
info.summary: Growing speakers join sentences with connecting words. They describe scenes with details, retell stories with a problem and solution, explain science and math steps, and give opinions with two reasons.
canDo: I can describe a scene with details and connecting words.
I can tell a story with a beginning, a problem, and an ending.
I can explain steps and causes using because and so.
I can give an opinion with two reasons.

categories.title: Describe Scenes
categories.desc: Describe places and people with connected details.

categories.title: Narrate Stories
categories.desc: Tell stories in order with connecting words.

categories.title: Explain How and Why
categories.desc: Explain science and math with because and steps.

activities.title: A Morning at the Market
activities.skill: Describe a scene with details
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the community market. Plan, then record your answer.
activities.prompt: Describe the market. Tell what each stand sells and what the people are doing.

picture.alt: An outdoor community market with three stands. The fruit stand sells apples for 50¢ each and bananas. The vegetable stand sells corn for 25¢ each and carrots. The bread stand sells loaves of bread for $2 each. A seller stands behind each stand. A mother and her son buy apples, and a man carries a shopping bag.

sayFor: the three stands and what they sell
connecting words: and, also, next to
vocabulary: the people and places in the area where you live
comunidad: las personas y lugares del área donde vives
frames: The mother and her son are ___.
activities.responsePlaceholder: At the first stand, ___. Next to it, ___.

models.B: The market has three stands. One stand sells apples and bananas, and the next one sells corn and carrots. A mother and her son are buying apples.
models.C: This picture shows a busy community market with three stands. The fruit stand sells apples for 50 cents and bananas too. Next to it, the vegetable stand has corn and carrots, and the bread stand sells loaves for two dollars. A mother and her son are buying apples, while a man walks by with a shopping bag. It looks like a friendly place where neighbors shop together.

activities.correct: Strong describing! You named the stands and the people. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Go from left to right: first stand, next stand, last stand.
activities.support: Model: The first stand sells fruit. The next stand sells vegetables. The last stand sells bread.
activities.extension: Tell about a market or store in your neighborhood.

teacher.use: Social Studies: community places and economics vocabulary.
teacher.function: Describe a scene with organized detail.
teacher.lower: Student names the three foods and repeats one frame per stand.
teacher.onLevel: Student describes all three stands and one person.
teacher.challenge: Student adds prices and a concluding sentence.
teacher.noTech: Set up a pretend market; students describe it to a partner.
teacher.prompt: What does the middle stand sell? Who is buying apples?

activities.title: The Rainy Picnic
activities.skill: Narrate a picture story with connecting words
activities.directions: Look at the three pictures. Plan, then tell the story.
activities.prompt: Tell the story of the family's picnic. Tell what happened and how the problem was solved.

picture.alt: A picture story in three parts. 1: Under a sunny sky, a mother and two children carry a picnic basket to the park. 2: Dark clouds come and rain falls on their picnic blanket, so they run. 3: At home, the family eats the picnic on a blanket on the living room floor while rain falls outside the window.

sayFor: order words: first, then, after that, finally
vocabulary: a meal you eat outside, often on a blanket
pícnic: comida que comes afuera, a menudo sobre una manta
find an answer to a problem
resolver: encontrar una solución a un problema
activities.responsePlaceholder: First, ___. Then, ___, so ___. Finally, ___.

models.A: They go to a picnic. It rains.
models.B: First, the family went to the park for a picnic. Then it started to rain, so they ran home. Finally, they had the picnic on the floor at home.
models.C: One sunny morning, a mother and her two children carried a picnic basket to the park. Then dark clouds came, and rain started to fall on their blanket, so everyone ran. They were sad at first because their picnic was ruined. However, when they got home, they spread the blanket on the living room floor. Finally, they had a cozy picnic inside while the rain fell outside.

activities.correct: Great storytelling! You told the problem and how the family solved it. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Each picture is one part of the story: beginning, problem, solution.
activities.support: Model: First, they went to the park. Then it rained. Finally, they ate at home.
activities.extension: Tell about a time your plans changed because of the weather.

teacher.use: Narrative with problem/solution, like the ACCESS narrate task.
teacher.function: Narrate events with sequence and cause words.
teacher.lower: Student says one sentence per panel using the first frame.
teacher.onLevel: Student uses then, so, and finally in past tense.
teacher.challenge: Student adds feelings and the word however.
teacher.noTech: Act out the story in three freeze frames, then narrate.
teacher.prompt: What was the problem? How did they solve it?

activities.title: Sun or No Sun?
activities.skill: Explain the results of an experiment
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the plant experiment. Plan, then record your answer.
activities.prompt: Explain what happened to Plant A and Plant B. Why are they different?

picture.alt: A science experiment with two bean plants. Plant A sits next to a sunny window and is tall with green leaves. Plant B sits inside a dark closet and is short with yellow, drooping leaves. A calendar on the wall has 14 days crossed out.

vocabulary: a test to find out something
light that comes from the sun
luz solar: luz que viene del sol
bend down because it is weak
marchitarse/caerse: doblarse hacia abajo por estar débil
activities.responsePlaceholder: Plant A is ___ because ___. Plant B is ___ because ___.

models.A: Plant A is big. Plant B is small.
models.B: Plant A is tall and green because it is next to the sunny window. Plant B is short and yellow because it was in a dark closet.

The bread stand sells loaves of bread for $2 each. A seller stands behind each stand. A mother and her son buy apples, and a man carries a shopping bag.

sayFor: what you will buy and how many
vocabulary: the amount when you add everything
total: la cantidad cuando sumas todo
money you get back when you pay too much
cambio/vuelto: dinero que te devuelven cuando pagas de más
a plan for how to spend money
presupuesto: plan de cómo gastar el dinero
frames: The total is ___, so I will have ___ left.
activities.responsePlaceholder: I will buy ___. That costs ___. The total is ___.

models.B: I will buy one loaf of bread for $2 and four apples. The apples cost $2 because 4 times 50 cents is $2. The total is $4, so I have $1 left.
models.C: With my five dollars, I will buy one loaf of bread, four apples, and four ears of corn. The bread costs $2.00, and four apples cost $2.00 because 4 times 50 cents equals 200 cents. Four ears of corn cost $1.00, since 4 times 25 cents is 100 cents. My total is exactly $5.00, so I will have no change left. I chose these foods because they are healthy, and there is enough for everyone in my family.

activities.correct: Great math reasoning! You explained prices, the total, and your choices. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Write each price first. Then add as you go and stop before you pass $5.00.
activities.support: Model: I will buy bread for $2. I will buy 2 apples for $1. That is $3. I have $2 left.
activities.extension: Make a different plan that leaves exactly $1.00 in change.

teacher.use: Math: money, multiplication, and addition; explaining reasoning.

activities.title: The Life Cycle of a Plant
activities.skill: Explain a cycle with academic vocabulary
activities.directions: Look at the four pictures of the pots. Plan, then explain the plant's life cycle.
activities.prompt: Explain the life cycle of a flowering plant. Tell what happens at each stage and what the plant needs.

picture.alt: Four pots in a row show how a plant grows. First, a seed is planted in the soil and watered. Next, a small sprout with two leaves comes up. Then, the plant grows taller with more leaves in the sun. Last, a yellow flower opens.

sayFor: science words: germinate, roots, stem, flower
vocabulary: when a seed starts to grow
germinar: cuando una semilla empieza a crecer
etapa: un paso en un ciclo
steps that happen again and again in a circle
ciclo: pasos que pasan una y otra vez en círculo
frames: The plant needs ___ in order to ___.
activities.responsePlaceholder: The life cycle begins when ___. During the next stage, ___.

models.A: A seed grows into a flower.
models.B: First, the seed is planted and gets water, and then it germinates into a sprout. Next, the plant grows taller with more leaves. Finally, it makes a flower.
models.C: The life cycle of a plant begins when a seed is planted in soil and watered. During the next stage, the seed germinates and a small sprout with two leaves pushes up. Then the stem grows taller and makes more leaves, because the plant uses sunlight and water to make food. In the last stage, a flower opens, and later the flower makes new seeds. That is how the cycle starts all over again.

activities.correct: Excellent! You explained each stage with science words. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Use one science word for each picture: seed, germinate, stem, flower.
activities.support: Model: The seed is planted. It germinates. The stem grows. The flower opens.
activities.extension: Compare the plant life cycle to the life cycle of a butterfly.

teacher.use: Science: life cycles; academic vocabulary in extended speech.
teacher.function: Explain a cycle with precise vocabulary.
teacher.lower: Student labels each stage with a word card and says it.
teacher.onLevel: Student explains all stages with order words.
teacher.challenge: Student explains how the cycle repeats and why the plant needs light.
teacher.noTech: Students draw the cycle as a circle and explain it to a partner.
teacher.prompt: What happens after the flower opens?

activities.title: How Many Books?
activities.skill: Argue an opinion with reasons and a counterargument
activities.directions: Read the question. Plan, then record your opinion.
activities.prompt: Right now, students can take home 2 library books at a time. Should students be allowed to take home 5 books? Explain your opinion.
sayFor: what someone on the other side might say
vocabulary: permitir: dejar que alguien haga algo
responsable: que cuida bien las cosas
a word that shows a different idea
sin embargo: palabra que muestra una idea diferente
activities.responsePlaceholder: I believe ___. One reason is ___. However, ___.

models.B: I believe students should take home five books because we read fast. Also, we can share books with our brothers and sisters.
models.C: I believe students should be allowed to take home five books. One reason is that many kids finish two books in just a few days and then have nothing to read. Another reason is that we could share books with younger brothers and sisters at home. Some people think more books will get lost. However, students can sign a promise to be responsible. In conclusion, five books would help everyone read more.

activities.correct: Convincing! You gave reasons and answered the other side. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Decide yes or no first. Then think of two reasons and one worry the other side has.
activities.support: Model: Yes, we should take five books. We read a lot. We can share. That is why I say yes.
activities.extension: Give your opinion on a different school rule, such as longer recess.

teacher.use: Opinion speaking with counterargument; Language Arts reading habits.
teacher.function: Argue with reasons and a counterargument.
teacher.lower: Student says yes or no with one reason using because.
teacher.onLevel: Student gives two reasons and a conclusion.
teacher.challenge: Student includes a counterargument with however.
teacher.noTech: Philosophical chairs: students move to yes/no sides and explain.
teacher.prompt: What might the other side say? How did you answer it?

activities.title: Plan Field Day

activities.directions: Look at the two weather pictures. Plan, then record your recommendation.
activities.prompt: Your school must choose a day for outdoor field day. Compare the weather in the two pictures and recommend which day is better. Explain what students should bring.

picture.alt: Two weather scenes. On the left, the sun shines in a blue sky and a boy in a T-shirt and shorts flies a kite. On the right, dark clouds drop rain, and a girl in a yellow raincoat and boots holds an umbrella next to a puddle.

sayFor: compare the two kinds of weather
compare words: while, but, on the other hand
vocabulary: say what you think is the best choice

frames: On the sunny day, ___, while on the rainy day, ___.
activities.responsePlaceholder: On the sunny day, ___, while ___. I recommend ___ because ___.

models.B: The sunny day is better for field day because kids can run and play outside. On the rainy day, the grass is wet and kids need umbrellas. Students should bring water.
models.C: On the sunny day, the sky is clear and a boy can even fly a kite, while on the rainy day, dark clouds drop rain and make puddles. I recommend the sunny day for field day because students can run races safely on dry grass. On the other hand, the rainy day could make the field slippery and dangerous. Students should bring water bottles and hats so that they stay cool in the sun.

activities.correct: Smart recommendation! You compared and gave reasons. Listen to the three sample answers to hear how a short answer grows into a longer one.
activities.hint: Tell one thing about each picture. Then pick one and say why.
activities.support: Model: The sunny day is dry. The rainy day is wet. I pick the sunny day. Bring water.
activities.extension: Suggest an indoor activity for the rainy day.

teacher.use: Science: weather and safety; comparing and recommending.

teacher.lower: Student says sunny/rainy and picks one day.
teacher.onLevel: Student compares and recommends with because.

activities.title: Why Communities Need Markets

activities.prompt: Explain how a market like this one helps a community. Use details from the picture and give at least two ways.

picture.alt: An outdoor community market with three stands. The fruit stand sells apples for 50¢ each and bananas. The vegetable stand sells corn for 25¢ each and carrots. frames: A market helps a community because ___.
activities.responsePlaceholder: A market helps a community because ___. For example, ___. Another way is ___.

models.B: A market helps a community because people can buy fresh food like apples and corn. Also, the sellers make money for their families.

activities.title: Best Answer: Field Trip Opinion
activities.skill: Choose the most developed spoken opinion
activities.directions: Look at the two pictures of field trip choices. Read the answers. Choose the strongest spoken answer.
activities.prompt: The teacher asks: Which field trip should our class take? Explain your opinion.

picture.alt: Two field trip choices side by side. On the left is a farm with a red barn, a cow, and two chickens behind a fence. On the right is an aquarium with a big glass tank of fish, a sea turtle, and two students looking in.

vocabulary: make an idea bigger with more details

frames: In my opinion, ___. First, ___. Also, ___. That is why ___.

options.text: The farm, because cows.

In my opinion, we should go to the farm. First, we can see where milk and eggs come from, like the cow and chickens. Also, we can walk outside and learn about animal care. That is why the farm is the best trip.
I want to go to both places because they are both fun and I like animals and fish and turtles.

activities.correct: Yes! This answer gives an opinion, two reasons with details from the picture, transitions, and a conclusion.
activities.hint: Find the answer that picks ONE place and explains it with First, Also, and That is why.

activities.title: Strong Reason or Weak Reason?
activities.skill: Judge whether a reason supports an opinion
activities.directions: Read the opinion and each reason. Sort each reason as strong or weak.
activities.prompt: Opinion: Our school should have a class garden. Sort each reason.
sayFor: reasons that explain with facts or examples
reasons that are more than just a feeling
vocabulary: help show that an idea is right
apoyar: ayudar a mostrar que una idea es correcta

items.text: Students can learn how plants grow by taking care of them.
We could grow vegetables to use in the school kitchen.
Working in a garden gets students outside and moving.

activities.correct: Great thinking! Strong reasons explain how or why with facts or examples.
activities.hint: Ask: Does this reason explain WHY a garden would help the school?
activities.support: Model: 'Students can learn how plants grow' is strong. 'Gardens are cool' is weak because it does not explain.
activities.extension: Turn one weak reason into a strong reason and say it aloud.

teacher.use: Builds the habit of supporting opinions with relevant reasons.

teacher.challenge: Student explains why each weak reason is weak.
